description: The true path of The Will in the Bible told from its data (the same moves): a will read as a paper of its own, its date and the christening it speaks of set against the parish register; with the testatrix dead before the christening and the housekeeper away and the loser by it, the nephew who held the keys.

moves.why: The will says it was made on the third of March.

moves.see: spoke of Thomas Pym as christened
moves.why: And it speaks of holding Thomas at the font.

moves.see: gave all she had to Mr. Lionel Pym
moves.why: The new will revokes the old and leaves all to Mr. Pym.

moves.see: had the keys of Ashcombe House
moves.why: Since her death the keys were Mr. Pym's.
Mrs. Grice was at Frome from the day after the funeral.

moves.see: gave Ashcombe House to Mrs. Grice
moves.why: And the new will would rob her of the house.
Thomas was christened on the first of July.
A will of March cannot speak of a christening in July.
Not on the third of March.
The will speaks of the christening.
Miss Pym died on the second of May.
Away, and the loser by it.
The one who had the keys, and gains everything.
